messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — started canary rollout of new rate-cap policy (policy id ratecap/v3/2026-03-15) to us-west-2 (10% hosts) at ~13:15Z. ACME support just reported a spike of 429s around 13:20. Ticket INC-4091. Can someone triage?

Morgan Patel: Thanks Alex — I'm on it. Spinning up a repro using the customer's embedding fanout pattern. Can you confirm what changed in the policy?

Alex Chen: The big change was reducing the per-key burst window from 60s -> 20s and adding a hard per-user concurrency cap. No other changes to global limits.

Morgan Patel: Repro curl I'm using (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-micro","input":"payload","n":6}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 429
Body: { "code": "rate_exceeded", "retry_after": 12 }

Ida Lopez: Copy. Can you capture the failing request headers (x-rl-remaining, x-rl-reset) and link to the canary grafana panel for us-west?

Morgan Patel: Pasted log snippet: `x-rl-remaining: 0`, `x-rl-reset: 23`, `x-rl-limit: 120`. Grafana (canary): https://grafana.internal/d/q123/canary-us-west-2 — panel shows QPS spike from ACME's key at 13:19.

Ida Lopez: Looks like the customer's fanout (6 concurrent embedding requests per user) interacts badly with 20s burst window; their short bursts exceed the allowance. Two immediate options: (1) rollback canary hosts to previous policy (60s), or (2) add a per-customer exception bumping their burst window to 60s while we investigate. Which do we want?

Jin Park: We support per-customer exceptions via policy service. Example patch: 
```
PATCH /admin/policies/ratecap/v3/2026-03-15
{ "exceptions": [{ "customer_id": "acme", "burst_window_sec": 60 }] }
```
I can apply that now; changes propagate in ~30s. We can also increase canary host burst capacity by +20% as a temporary buffer.

Alex Chen: ACME is on a paid plan and wants a fast fix. Please apply the exception and let the customer know. If capacity risks spike across canary, we'll rollback.

deploy-bot: rollout started ratecap/v3/2026-03-15 -> us-west-2 (10%) by Alex Chen at 2026-03-15T13:16:42Z

Morgan Patel: Applying exception now. Patching policy service.

policy-service: exception patched for customer acme by Morgan Patel at 2026-03-15T13:17:20Z

Morgan Patel: Confirmed — ACME requests accepted again, no more 429s in the test window. Headers now show `x-rl-remaining: 38`. Updated customer in INC-4091.

Jin Park: Also increased canary host burst capacity +20% temporarily. Watching GPU queue length and concurrency; will revert if we see cross-tenant impact.

Ida Lopez: Monitoring p50/p95 latency and token QPS. After 10 minutes metrics look stable; no meaningful tail-latency regression and canary utilization within targets. If utilization >85% of canary capacity we will rollback.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. Notes for postmortem: the reduced burst window had an unintended effect on high-fanout embedding workflows. Action items: (1) add a pre-rollout smoke test that simulates fanout workloads, (2) update rollout checklist to include a per-customer exception path and quick patch steps, (3) run cost/impact analysis for exception usage.

Morgan Patel: Filing follow-up: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4091 — I'll attach repro artifacts and sample logs. Closing thread once postmortem notes are in. :white_check_mark:
